revision_summary: No quote fabrications were found — all quotes check out against the transcript. The core issue is a speaker-role ambiguity that Stage 3 identifies but does not resolve or flag prominently enough. The transcript's diarization labels ('rep' and 'customer') appear inverted from the standard Ion setter-call pattern: the person labeled 'customer' opens by confirming 'Yeah. Yeah. This is Ion Solar' and proceeds to look up the appointment record, propose reschedule dates, and confirm the address back to the caller — behaviors consistent with the Ion rep, not the homeowner. The person labeled 'rep' is the one who called in about a missed appointment, mentions his own work schedule and shift-based job, and is referred to by name as 'Gregory' when the record is pulled — consistent with the customer/homeowner role. Stage 3 catches this in a single cherry_pick_moment ('Likely a diarization artifact') but then proceeds to build its entire trajectory_verdict, state_changes, script_coverage, and handoff_brief on the literal (likely incorrect) speaker labels without flagging the inversion at the top of the analysis or reconciling it. On rerun: (1) State explicitly and early in the analysis (e.g., in starting_state or a dedicated note) that the diarization roles appear swapped, with the reasoning laid out (the 'customer'-labeled speaker confirms the company name, pulls records, and drives the reschedule logistics; the 'rep'-labeled speaker is identified by name as Gregory and describes being called into work). (2) Either re-run all downstream sections against corrected roles, or if uncertain, caveat every quote attribution accordingly so a manager reading script_coverage and handoff_brief understands who actually said what. (3) Clarify the button_up schema citations to reference the specific missing sub-elements rather than bundling multiple distinct button_up failures under a single is_that_fair_handshake citation. The trajectory_verdict's outcome dispute (tentative vs. booked) is well-supported and should be preserved as-is once speaker roles are clarified.
